registry: Content Hubs — registry and recorded keyword strategies
source_of_record: Content Hubs 2 tab (dash index) — hub cards, keyword sections, embedded product digest snapshot 2026-10-18
definition: The keyword strategy of a hub is defined by the current organization of clusters and topics in the keyword sections of the Content Hubs 2 tab, recorded here.
note_model_agnostic: A hub's keyword strategy is the recorded organization of clusters and topics in the keyword sections of the Content Hubs 2 tab, as captured in this registry. Arranging, adding, or removing clusters or topics in that tab constitutes a change to the hub's recorded keyword strategy, and this registry must be re-recorded to match. Each hub has fidelity to exactly one campaign, and the campaign sits upstream of the hub. Any model or tool working in this system must treat this registry as the keyword strategy of record, surface rearrangements as strategy changes for the operator's decision, and never silently reorganize clusters or topics. AI is a filter, not a source: rearrangement proposals are options for the operator, not edits to apply unilaterally. Amendment (operator decision, Oct 20, 2026): the CAMPAIGN is the authority and replaces the hub as the top form in the flow. Hubs are separate entities from campaigns, tracked in their own registry; they are not assets and sit outside the flow. Hubs no longer hold keywords: each hub's main keywords move onto its campaign's Keywords field, and campaign research re-runs off those main keywords, recording an SEO strategy. The keyword strategy of record is therefore the campaign's: its main keywords on the campaign record plus the cluster/topic organization recorded in this registry (re-recorded under the campaign).
